summary: Populate the live search response path so search.messages hits are unwrapped from Slack's nested envelope.
reason: The generator left searchResponsePaths empty, so extractSearchResults fell through every generic wrapper key ("data", "results", "items", "records", "entries") and returned the whole response as a single item. search.messages answers {"ok":true,"messages":{"total":N,"matches":[...],"paging":{...}}}, so a query with N hits yielded exactly one result — the envelope itself, rendered as a row with no text, ts or permalink — while the N real matches stayed buried inside it. Note this is a different symptom from the same defect on the pre-reprint tree, where the envelope was additionally discarded by isNilOrEmpty and the command printed "No results" and exited 0; the reprint's generic hasAnyNonEmptySearchValue recurse now keeps the envelope, so the failure presents as one garbage row rather than silence. Because that recurse also keeps a real match on its text/ts/permalink fields, naming the dotted path is the entire fix on this tree — the hand-rolled envelope struct and the isNilOrEmpty match-recognition that the pre-reprint patch needed are both unnecessary now.
validated_outcome: Negative control run explicitly rather than assumed: on a realistic two-match envelope, extractSearchResults with the path returns 2 items, and without it returns 1 — which survives isNilOrEmpty and would have been rendered as a result. Four unit cases pass (unwraps matches, matches survive the nil-or-empty filter, the full live pipeline keeps them, an empty result set stays empty). responsePayloadAtPath resolves the dotted path, so no new traversal code was added. `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `go test ./...` clean.
upstream: The generator knows the endpoint has a search response schema — it emits the extractSearchResults call and the searchResponsePaths variable — but leaves the paths empty instead of deriving them from the spec's response shape. Deriving the array-valued path (here messages.matches) would fix this class for every API whose search results are nested rather than top-level, instead of leaving a variable that looks configured and is not.
